classification: heuristic numerical test of a formulation question (no certification)
connection_to_goal: Decides whether the sup over boundary data V in Deep's (H1) can hold: a negative Hessian direction inside the fibre of a uniform-field V means the uniform field is a saddle, the fibre measure at weak coupling sits on a degenerate non-uniform family, and sup-over-V decay is not the right target.
cpu_baseline: Hessian assembly is 256 plaquettes x 78 pair stencils of 2x2 products; eigen and null-space of 1536x1536 dense matrices; minutes per flux value.
decision_rule: If ker J carries negative Hessian directions for admissible n at b=8 (and especially for the 'all' block map), record sup-over-V (H1) as unsupported and restate H1 in averaged form; if never negative, record that this obstruction does not apply.
expected_result: free_neg > 0 for every n>0 (Nielsen-Olesen); on ker J, negatives appear once the flux quanta exceed roughly the constraint count 6L^2/b^2, i.e. for b=8 around n>12, not for b=2.
question: Does the uniform abelian chromomagnetic background, restricted to its block-map fibre, have a negative Hessian direction for SU(2) Wilson action?
resource_justification: single process numpy/scipy, 4 CPUs for BLAS, 8 GB for dense 1536^2 matrices, 2 h cap.
stop_rule: Run once; if background checks (plaq_dev, grad_max) are not ~1e-8 or the n=0 case shows negatives, stop and fix the script before resubmitting.
